issues.claim: `CommandManager.RequerySuggested` holds its handlers only through weak references, and the documentation warns that the caller must keep a strong reference to the handler.
issues.problem: This comes from the CommandManager.RequerySuggested API remarks. Neither linked page nor either excerpt shows it, yet the text says 'the documentation'. It is probably true, but the cited sources do not support it.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the CommandManager.RequerySuggested API page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.input.commandmanager.requerysuggested) to `links`, with a matching `linkTitles` entry in both locales, or remove the example.

issues.claim: The handler must be a method of an object that something else keeps alive, otherwise the subscription can disappear together with the listener.
issues.problem: No linked source or excerpt states this. It rests on WeakEventManager internals (weak reference to the handler target), as the generator notes admit. The lambda/closure pitfall is stated as fact without support.
issues.suggestedFix: Support it with a source that states it, or rephrase as a caveat: 'the manager does not keep the handler target alive, so a lambda whose closure is referenced only by the handler can be collected early; use a method on the listener object'.

issues.claim: Release is non-deterministic: until the next garbage collection the handler of a closed screen can still be called.
issues.problem: Correct, but the excerpts do not show it. The 'Purge/ScheduleCleanup' cleanup is visible on the API page only as method descriptions.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally cite the WeakEventManager page (ScheduleCleanup/Purge) next to this sentence, or leave it as a reasoned consequence of weak references.
